## Problem

A standards-mapped claim is only as good as the run evidence each
control row carries. The example claim: "this deployment verifies at
AISVS 1.0
level 2 / the OWASP LLM Top 10 / MLSVS". Today Kailash ships NO
verifier
tooling: the pre-#210 D-7 surface (`kailash verifier`) mapped to
toolkit rows whose claimed upstream repositories were never created. The
os#210 audit removed all of them
([os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210); the
standards THEMSELVES are real and published). The task: an evidence
chain for control claims that is honest NOW, using only real tools.

## Solution

Assemble the control statement from what exists today — run records +
the published standards + the manifest's own mapping fields:

```bash
# 0. Confirm your lab surface ran at ALL (the input to any mapping):
#    e.g. [Attack the platform, then verify](../attack-defence/attack-then-verify.html)
#    leaves a --record JSON (real, verbatim-backed); a garak run leaves a
#    .jsonl report. A control statement without run evidence is a wish.

# 1. Pin the run to the tool row (the manifest is the mapping record):
kailash info garak | grep -i -A4 owasp
#    -> the row's owasp_llm map (both epochs)
kailash info garak | grep -i atlas
#    -> the row's ATLAS technique ids

# 2. Open the standard you are mapping TO (published, upstream):
#      AISVS 1.0: https://github.com/OWASP/AISVS (levels + ASVS alignment)
#      OWASP LLM Top 10 (2026 + v2:2025 epochs)
#    Read the requirement text from the standard, NEVER a hand-copy.

# 3. Bind the run: your report's citation skeleton per control —
#      "control <requirement-id> (AISVS 1.0, level 2): exercised by
#       garak --spec tag:owasp:llm01 (report <file>, tool pin <rev>),
#       target <endpoint>, recorded <date>"
#    the run record makes it REPRODUCIBLE; the tool pin makes it
#    RE-RUNNABLE; the standard's requirement text makes it CHECKABLE.

# 4. State the level (or epochs) explicitly in every downstream
#    citation — it is part of the claim, not a knob.
```

What success looks like:

- every rendered control statement traces to a manifest field or a
  published standard clause
- no hand-copied control text sits anywhere
- the report's citation names the standard + level, the tool + pin,
  the run record, and the date
- all four, or the claim is unfinished
- `kailash manifest validate` stays green (the mapping's ground truth
  is the same manifest the CLI bakes)

## Discussion

- **The verifier CLI is aspirational-only:** the verifier-CLI row, the
  three standards toolkit packs, and the
  ASVS toolkit ride the
  [os#210 registry](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210).
  None was ever built. When a verifier ships via the rebuild
  contract, this recipe re-opens with real `kailash verifier`
  invocations per the spec's standard-first mode.
- **What a verified control statement looks like (now):** a
  requirement-id, a mechanism, and run-reproduction. "AISVS 1.0
  §<chapter/id> level 2 — verified by <tool> <version> against
  <target/record> on <date>" — with the record itself attached (a
  garak JSONL, an mlflow-pair --record JSON). The book's
  no-invented-evidence rule applies: a claim with no verbatim run
  behind it is not evidence.
- **Level choice is a posture decision, not a decoration:** AISVS
  levels are ascending depth-of-assurance per requirement. Pick the
  level the AUTHORISATION context demands (e.g. IRAP/ISM-mapped work
  wants the higher levels evidenced, not just level 1) and STATE it
  in every downstream citation.
- **LLM Top 10 has two epochs:** the manifest's owasp_llm field maps
  both `{2026: ...}` and `{v2: ...}` per row — a report naming only
  one epoch is incomplete for any audience spanning the
  v2:2025 → 2026 transition.
- **NIST/ISO governance packs are also registry riders:** the D-6
  packs (ISO/IEC 42001 AIMS, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act) were
  phantom-origin rows, removed — see
  [os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210).
  Governance-work products wait on the rebuild contract; the
  TECHNICAL verification leg above is real today.
